narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 17 % chance you won’t pass your final year, which is above the 10 % threshold the school uses to require extra help. That’s why you’re being asked to take remedial courses.

The three factors that mattered most in the prediction are, first, that you’ve never failed a class before. This is actually working in your favor—it’s the strongest reason the model thinks you can still succeed. Second, you’ve said you want to go on to higher education; this ambition is also pushing the prediction toward passing. Third, your father’s education level is helping too, because students whose fathers have a higher-education background tend to do better.

On the other hand, some of your habits are nudging the prediction the other way. You told us you study less than two hours a week, which is below what most students who pass report. You also spend a lot of free time going out with friends, and while that’s normal, it can leave less room for schoolwork. The model sees these patterns and raises the estimated risk.

The good news is that the factors that are already helping you—no past failures, clear university plans, and a supportive home—are strong. If you can add a little more study time and balance your social life, you’ll give yourself the best chance to finish the year successfully. The remedial courses are there to help you do exactly that.
